notes: The San Francisco Call's Saturday Real Estate and Financial Section for January to June 1910, from curiv_jenner_ver01 and curiv_klamath_ver01 (the whole of 1910 is on disk across jenner, klamath, mecca and needles; July to December was not read). In 1910 the section runs three pages: the page headed REAL ESTATE AND FINANCIAL SECTION and the two after it, up to the bay-counties news; special Richmond and Turlock editions push it later in the issue on 5 March and 30 April. 26 Saturdays, 84 OCR pages. 1910 is after the 1909 renumbering, so every entry carries extra.record_date. The building-news column is far denser than in 1912 or 1913 - about 150 architect or corner passages in six months against 27 unnumbered entries in all of 1912 - so this batch takes the numbered entries and the corner or offset entries that name an architect, a building, an institution or a firm; permits naming only a private owner and no architect are left for a later corner.py batch. Taken: numbered sales, offerings and leases that say something about the building (its form, rooms, lot, a firm that took it), and buildings located by corner, offset or name, placed by hand with research/tools/corner.py on lot area, storeys and roll year. Left out at extraction: private buyers, sellers, lessors, lessees and owners (the raw quotes are cut or spliced round their names), the metes-and-bounds Real Estate Transactions list, the country-land and Oakland pages, and advertisers' own offices.

coverage.remaining: July to December 1910 (26 Saturdays, curiv_klamath_ver01 from July, curiv_mecca_ver01 and curiv_needles_ver01) is on disk in a session that fetched it and unread. In January to June, the building-contract and permit paragraphs that name only a private owner and no architect (roughly 150 corner and offset entries) were not taken; they are the next corner.py batch. The Real Estate Transactions lists are metes-and-bounds and were not read for entries.
coverage.note: 393 numbered-address mentions on the 84 pages, merged into 268 passages, and about 150 passages naming an architect or a corner, read one by one. About a third of the numbered mentions are brokers' and advertisers' own offices, and many are Oakland, Richmond, the peninsula or the Central Valley. 172 findings: 76 at a street number, 96 located by corner, offset or building name; 76 resolved (45 by hand), 96 unresolved, most because the building has been replaced and nothing of the period survives on the corner, or the number no longer exists; 73 published on 68 pages, 28 of them seeded; 3 declined as duplicates of what the page already carried.
